text: Cito, workflow preparing complex data Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) Multimodal Neural Networks (MMNs) . difference MMNs can process multiple data types simultaneously (see ‘MMN’ section ). dive details, let’s clarify represent different types complex data R using multidimensional arrays: Black/white image: [height,width][height, width] height/width number pixels Colored images: [3,height,width][3, height, width] 3 channels three colors LiDAR point clouds: [x,y,z][x, y, z] Environmental time series (can also represented “image”): [time_steps,n_covariates][\text{time_steps}, \text{n_covariates}] Note: Cito currently supports three-dimensional inputs (excluding sample dimension). Four-dimensional arrays, temporal RGB sequences [3,height,width,timesteps][3, height, width, time_steps], yet supported. Please contact us need support 4D inputs.

what: Linear effects and embeddings in the formula
title: Introduction to cito
text: Two special terms extend formula. fe() adds predictors linear effects, added output network link scale, model η=f(X)+βTxfe\eta = f(X) + \beta^T x_{fe} ff neural network. β\beta estimated together network, like parametric term GAM. fe() takes right-hand side formula, terms (Temp^2), interactions factors work lm(). variables fe() passed network, . expands variables. fixed effects intercept (network one), affected lambda alpha dnn(); can regularized fe(..., lambda = , alpha = ). β\beta close GLM coefficient training converged fixed-effect variables functions network inputs. correlated network inputs, strongly regularized network can bias β\beta. coef() gives standard errors; fit bootstrap = see spread. e() adds embedding categorical variable (e.g. site individual), learned part input network. Precp enters network although true effect linear; variable can enter either network fe(), . mmn() custom networks fe() available yet.
code: set.seed(42) n = 1000 sim = data.frame(X1 = runif(n, -2, 2), Temp = rnorm(n), Precp = rnorm(n),                  Site = factor(sample(paste0("site", 1:10), n, replace = TRUE))) site_effect = rnorm(10, sd = 0.5) sim$Y = sin(2 * sim$X1) + 1.0 * sim$Temp - 0.5 * sim$Temp^2 + 0.5 * sim$Precp +   site_effect[sim$Site] + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3)  fit_fe = dnn(Y ~ X1 + Precp + fe(Temp + I(Temp^2)) + e(Site, dim = 2),              data = sim, loss = "mse", epochs = 100, verbose = FALSE, plot = FALSE)  # the linear effects, simulated as 1.0 and -0.5 coef(fit_fe)$fixed_effects #>                 [,1] #> Temp       1.0243872 #> I(Temp^2) -0.5239018

text: Neural networks can used unconventional way optimize arbitrary functions (sometimes called active learning, related reinforcement learning) - prerequisite analytic derivative function using torch must available. provide function optimized series Torch operations. First, model predict parameters (based noise, inputs don’t matter) passed custom loss function use model function (optimize) compute loss return optimizer. way overfit noisy inputs DNN learn predict optimal set parameters - independent input.
code: X = runif(200) Y = 2*X + rnorm(200, sd = 0.4) df = data.frame(X = X, Y = Y)  # Function we want to optimize (linear model) Xt = torch_tensor(matrix(X)) Yt = torch_tensor(matrix(Y))  model_lm = function(par) {   pred = Xt$matmul(par[,1,drop=FALSE])   loss = -torch::distr_normal(pred, scale = torch::torch_exp(par[,2,drop=FALSE]))$log_prob(Yt)   return(loss$mean()) }  custom_loss = function(pred, true, ...) {   if(nrow(pred) > 1) return(torch_zeros(1L)) # disable loss calculation   loss = model_lm(pred)   return(loss) }  # X and Y values don't matter, number of columns in Y has to match the number of parameters we want to optimize noise = matrix(runif(300*5), 300, 5) noise_y = matrix(runif(300*2), 300, 2) df = data.frame(y1 = noise_y[,1], y2 = noise_y[,2], noise)  m = dnn(cbind(y1, y2)~., data = df, loss = custom_loss, batchsize = 1L, epochs = 20L, verbose = FALSE) # Effect: mean(predict(m)[,1]) #> [1] 1.948921 # SD mean(exp(predict(m)[,2])) #> [1] 0.4207086

code: architecture_LiDAR <- create_architecture(transfer("resnet18")) architecture_RGBimages <- create_architecture(transfer("resnet18"))  model =   mmn(Y ~       cnn(X = LiDAR, architecture = architecture_LiDAR) +       cnn(X = RGBimages, architecture = architecture_RGBimages) +       dnn(~Temp+Precip, data = df),       dataList = list(Y = df$Y, LiDAR = LiDAR, RGBimages = RGBimages, df = df),       loss = 'binomial',       optimizer = "adam") model =   mmn(Y ~       cnn(X = LiDAR, architecture = architecture_LiDAR) +       cnn(X = RGBimages, architecture = architecture_RGBimages) +       dnn(~Temp+Precip, data = df),       dataList = list(Y = cbind(df$Y1, df$Y2, df$Y3), LiDAR = LiDAR,                       RGBimages = RGBimages, df = df),       loss = 'binomial',       optimizer = "adam") predict(model, newdata = list(LiDAR = LiDAR, RGBimages = RGBimages, df = df), type = "response") custom_joint_loss = function(pred, true) {    # first loss, e.g. binomial -> negative loglikelihood   loss1 = -torch::distr_bernoulli(logits = torch_sigmoid(pred[,1]))$log_prob(true[,1])$mean()    # second loss, e.g. mse   loss2 = torch::nnf_mse_loss(pred[,2], true[,2])    # third loss, e.g. poisson   loss3 = -torch::distr_poisson(pred[,3]$exp())$log_prob(true[,3])$mean()    # return joint loss   return(loss1 + loss2 + loss3) }  model =   mmn(Y ~       cnn(X = LiDAR, architecture = architecture_LiDAR) +       cnn(X = RGBimages, architecture = architecture_RGBimages) +       dnn(~Temp+Precip, data = df),       dataList = list(Y = cbind(df$Y1, df$Y2, df$Y3), LiDAR = LiDAR,                       RGBimages = RGBimages, df = df),       loss = custom_joint_loss,       epochs = 5L,       optimizer = "adam") pred = predict(model, newdata = list(LiDAR = LiDAR, RGBimages = RGBimages, df = df)) pred[,1] = plogis(pred[,1]) pred[,3] = exp(pred[,3])

title: Create an Average Pooling Layer for a CNN Architecture — avgPool
code: avgPool(kernel_size = NULL, stride = NULL, padding = NULL)

title: Create an Average Pooling Layer for a CNN Architecture — avgPool
text: kernel_size (integer tuple) size kernel layer. Use tuple kernel size differs across dimensions. stride (integer tuple) stride kernel layer. NULL, stride set kernel size. Use tuple stride differs across dimensions. padding (integer tuple) amount zero-padding added input sides. Use tuple padding differs across dimensions.

title: Create an Average Pooling Layer for a CNN Architecture — avgPool
text: S3 object class "avgPool" "citolayer", representing average pooling layer CNN architecture.

title: Create an Average Pooling Layer for a CNN Architecture — avgPool
text: function creates avgPool layer object, represents average pooling layer CNN architecture. Parameters specified (thus set NULL) filled default values provided create_architecture function.

title: Create an Average Pooling Layer for a CNN Architecture — avgPool
text: Armin Schenk

title: Create an Average Pooling Layer for a CNN Architecture — avgPool
code: # \donttest{ if(torch::torch_is_installed()){ library(cito)  # A average pooling layer where all available parameters are assigned # No value will be overwritten by 'create_architecture()' layer1 <- avgPool(3, 1, 0)  # A average pooling layer where only the kernel size is assigned # stride and padding are filled with the defaults # passed to the 'create_architecture()' function layer2 <- avgPool(kernel_size=4) } # }

what: 'cito': Building and training neural networks — cito
title: 'cito': Building and training neural networks — cito
text: 'cito' package provides user-friendly interface training interpreting deep neural networks (DNN). 'cito' simplifies fitting DNNs supporting familiar formula syntax, hyperparameter tuning cross-validation, helps detect handle convergence problems.  DNNs can trained CPU, GPU MacOS GPUs. addition, 'cito' many downstream functionalities various explainable AI (xAI) metrics (e.g. variable importance, partial dependence plots, accumulated local effect plots, effect estimates) interpret trained DNNs. 'cito' optionally provides confidence intervals (p-values) xAI metrics predictions. time, 'cito' computationally efficient based deep learning framework 'torch'. 'torch' package native R, Python installation API required package.

title: 'cito': Building and training neural networks — cito
text: Cito built around main function dnn, creates trains deep neural network. Various tools analyzing trained neural network available.

title: 'cito': Building and training neural networks — cito
text: order install cito please follow steps: install.packages("cito") library(torch) install_torch(reinstall = TRUE) library(cito)

title: 'cito': Building and training neural networks — cito
text: dnn: train deep neural network cnn, mmn: train convolutional multi-modal neural networks raster_patches: train cnn() mmn() windows read one large GeoTIFF analyze_training: check convergence comparing training loss baseline loss continue_training: continues training existing cito dnn model additional epochs summary.citodnn: extract xAI metrics/effects understand predictions made PDP: plot partial dependency plot specific feature ALE: plot accumulated local effect plot specific feature Check vignettes details training NN typical workflow 'cito' look like.

title: 'cito': Building and training neural networks — cito
code: # \donttest{  if(torch::torch_is_installed()){ library(cito)  # Example workflow in cito  ## Build and train  Network ### cross-entropy (softmax link) for multi-class responses (e.g., Species) nn.fit<- dnn(Species~., data = datasets::iris, loss = "cross-entropy")  ## The training loss is below the baseline loss but at the end of the ## training the loss was still decreasing, so continue training for another 50 ## epochs nn.fit <- continue_training(nn.fit, epochs = 50L)  # Structure of Neural Network print(nn.fit)  # Plot Neural Network if(requireNamespace("ggraph", quietly = TRUE)) plot(nn.fit, plot_type = "arch") ## 4 Input nodes (first layer) because of 4 features ## 3 Output nodes (last layer) because of 3 response species (one node for each ## level in the response variable). ## The layers between the input and output layer are called hidden layers (two ## of them)  ## We now want to understand how the predictions are made, what are the ## important features? The summary function automatically calculates feature ## importance (the interpretation is similar to an anova) and calculates ## average conditional effects that are similar to linear effects: summary(nn.fit)  ## To visualize the effect (response-feature effect), we can use the ALE and ## PDP functions  # Partial dependencies PDP(nn.fit, variable = "Petal.Length")  # Accumulated local effect plots ALE(nn.fit, variable = "Petal.Length")    # Per se, it is difficult to get confidence intervals for our xAI metrics (or # for the predictions). But we can use bootstrapping to obtain uncertainties # for all cito outputs: ## Re-fit the neural network with bootstrapping nn.fit<- dnn(Species~.,              data = datasets::iris,              loss = "cross-entropy",              epochs = 150L,              verbose = FALSE,              bootstrap = 20L) ## convergence can be tested via the analyze_training function analyze_training(nn.fit)  ## Summary for xAI metrics (can take some time): summary(nn.fit, importance = "permutation", type = "link") ## Now with standard errors and p-values ## Note: Take the p-values with a grain of salt! We do not know yet if they are ## correct (e.g. if you use regularization, they are likely conservative == too ## large)  ## Predictions with bootstrapping: dim(predict(nn.fit)) ## predictions are by default averaged (over the bootstrap samples)  ## Multinomial and conditional logit regression m = dnn(Species~., data = iris, loss = "clogit", lr = 0.01) m = dnn(Species~., data = iris, loss = "multinomial", lr = 0.01)  Y = t(stats::rmultinom(100, 10, prob = c(0.2, 0.2, 0.5))) m = dnn(cbind(X1, X2, X3)~., data = data.frame(Y, A = as.factor(runif(100))),         loss = "multinomial", lr = 0.01) ## conditional logit for size > 1 is not supported yet   # Hyperparameter tuning (experimental feature) hidden_values = matrix(c(5, 2,                          4, 2,                          10,2,                          15,2), 4, 2, byrow = TRUE) ## Potential architectures we want to test, first column == number of nodes print(hidden_values)  nn.fit = dnn(Species~.,              data = iris,              epochs = 30L,              loss = "cross-entropy",              hidden = tune(values = hidden_values),              lr = tune(0.00001, 0.1) # tune lr between range 0.00001 and 0.1              ) ## Tuning results: print(nn.fit$tuning)  # test = Inf means that tuning was cancelled after only one fit (within the CV)   # Advanced: Custom loss functions and additional parameters ## Normal Likelihood with sd parameter: custom_loss = function(pred, true) {   logLik = torch::distr_normal(pred,                                scale = torch::nnf_relu(scale)+                                  0.001)$log_prob(true)   return(-logLik$mean()) }  nn.fit<- dnn(Sepal.Length~.,              data = datasets::iris,              loss = custom_loss,              verbose = FALSE,              custom_parameters = list(scale = 1.0) ) nn.fit$loss$parameters$scale  ## Multivariate normal likelihood with parametrized covariance matrix ## Sigma = L*L^t + D ## Helper function to build covariance matrix create_cov = function(LU, Diag) {   return(torch::torch_matmul(LU, LU$t()) + torch::torch_diag(Diag$exp()+0.01)) }  custom_loss_MVN = function(true, pred) {   Sigma = create_cov(SigmaPar, SigmaDiag)   logLik = torch::distr_multivariate_normal(pred,                                             covariance_matrix = Sigma)$     log_prob(true)   return(-logLik$mean()) }   nn.fit<- dnn(cbind(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, Petal.Length)~.,              data = datasets::iris,              lr = 0.01,              verbose = FALSE,              loss = custom_loss_MVN,              custom_parameters =                list(SigmaDiag =  rep(0, 3),                     SigmaPar = matrix(rnorm(6, sd = 0.001), 3, 2)) ) as.matrix(create_cov(nn.fit$loss$parameters$SigmaPar,                      nn.fit$loss$parameters$SigmaDiag))   # Embeddings and fixed effects ## Species enters as an embedding: each species gets two learned coordinates, ## from which the network learns how the species differ in their response to ## all predictors. Petal.Width enters as a fixed (linear) effect. nn.fit = dnn(Sepal.Length ~ Sepal.Width + Petal.Length + fe(Petal.Width) + e(Species, dim = 2),              data = datasets::iris, loss = "mse", epochs = 50L, verbose = FALSE)  ## the linear effect of Petal.Width coef(nn.fit)$fixed_effects  ## the embeddings, one row per species coef(nn.fit)$net_parameters$e_1.weight  ## architecture: Species feeds its two embedding dimensions, Petal.Width goes ## straight to the output if(requireNamespace("ggraph", quietly = TRUE)) plot(nn.fit, plot_type = "arch") } #> Loss at epoch 1: 1.015505, lr: 0.01000  #> code: cnn(   X,   Y = NULL,   architecture = NULL,   custom = NULL,   loss = c("mse", "mae", "cross-entropy", "bernoulli", "gaussian", "binomial", "poisson",     "mvp", "nbinom", "multinomial", "clogit", "softmax"),   custom_parameters = NULL,   optimizer = c("sgd", "adam", "adadelta", "adagrad", "rmsprop", "rprop", "ignite_adam"),   lr = 0.01,   lr_scheduler = NULL,   alpha = 0.5,   lambda = 0,   validation = 0,   batchsize = NULL,   shuffle = TRUE,   data_augmentation = NULL,   num_workers = 0L,   num_threads = 4L,   epochs = 100,   weights = NULL,   early_stopping = Inf,   burnin = Inf,   baseloss = NULL,   device = c("cpu", "cuda", "mps"),   plot = TRUE,   verbose = TRUE )

title: Train a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) — cnn
text: X array input data minimum 3 maximum 5 dimensions. first dimension represents samples, second dimension represents channels, third fifth dimensions represent input dimensions. alternative, can provide relative absolute path folder containing images. case, unsigned integer images divided maximum value (255 8 bit, 65535 16 bit), floating point signed integer TIFFs passed unchanged. Windows one large raster given raster_patches. Y target data. allowed formats target data differ loss functions. See dnn information. architecture object class 'citoarchitecture'. See create_architecture information. Ignored custom provided. custom custom network architecture, replaces architecture argument. Either nn_module generator, instantiated nn_module, list(module = generator, args = list(...), output_dim = integer). initialize method arguments named input output, filled automatically (input = input shape, e.g. c(channels, height, width), output = output dimension expected loss). forward method receives float tensor shape (batch, input_shape) must return tensor shape (batch, output). See dnn details loss loss function used. Options include "mse", "mae", "cross-entropy", "bernoulli", "gaussian", "binomial", "poisson", "nbinom", "mvp", "multinomial", "clogit". can also specify loss function. See Details information. Default 0.01. lr_scheduler Learning rate scheduler. See config_lr_scheduler creating learning rate scheduler. Default NULL. alpha Alpha value L1/L2 regularization. Default 0.5. lambda Lambda value L1/L2 regularization. Default 0.0. validation Proportion data used validation. Alternatively, vector containing indices validation samples can provided. Default 0.0. batchsize Batch size training. NULL, batchsize 10% training data. Default NULL. shuffle Whether shuffle data epoch. Default TRUE. data_augmentation list functions used data augmentation. Elements must either functions strings corresponding inbuilt data augmentation functions. See details information. num_workers (integer) Number worker processes dataloader. effective folder inputs; raster inputs raster_patches always use 0 prefetch reader thread instead. 0 decodes main process. num_threads (integer) Number threads compiled image decoder uses per batch folder inputs, number reader threads raster inputs raster_patches. epochs Number epochs train model. Default 100. weights weights values (can also matrix) likelihood access early_stopping Number epochs improvement training stopped. Default Inf. burnin Number epochs training stops loss still baseloss. Default Inf. baseloss Baseloss used burnin plot. NULL, baseloss corresponds intercept models. Default NULL. device Device used training. Options "cpu", "cuda", "mps". Default "cpu". plot Whether plot training progress. Default TRUE. verbose Whether print detailed training progress. Default TRUE.

title: Train a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) — cnn
text: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) specialized type neural network designed processing structured data, images. key components CNN convolutional layers, pooling layers fully-connected (linear) layers: Convolutional layers core building blocks CNNs. consist filters (also called kernels), small, learnable matrices. filters slide input data perform element-wise multiplication, producing feature maps capture local patterns features. Multiple filters used detect different features parallel. help network learn hierarchical representations input data capturing low-level features (edges, textures) gradually combining (subsequent convolutional layers) form higher-level features. Pooling layers reduce size feature maps created convolutional layers, retaining important information. common type max pooling, keeps highest value region, simplifying data preserving essential features. Fully-connected (linear) layers connect every neuron one layer every neuron next layer. layers found end network responsible combining high-level features make final predictions. architecture CNN created trained function defined object class 'citoarchitecture'. See create_architecture detailed information define customize CNN architecture.

title: Train a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) — cnn
text: Data augmentation technique used improve generalization convolutional neural networks (CNNs) increasing diversity training data random transformations. function supports data augmentation data_augmentation argument, accepts list containing either user-defined functions names cito's built-data augmentation functions. user-defined function must take torch_tensor input return torch_tensor shape. input tensor must 3 5 dimensions following structure: Dimension 1: singleton batch dimension (.e., size 1), Dimension 2: channel dimension, Dimensions 3 5: spatial dimensions (e.g., X, Y, Z). training, data loader re-loads sample every epoch, applying provided augmentation functions sequentially time sample accessed. allows transformations vary across epochs functions include randomness (e.g., randomly flipping spatial axis) helping model learn invariance changes. addition custom functions, list can contain names (strings) following built-augmentation methods: "rotate90": 2D convolutions: randomly applies one 4 possible 90° rotations. X Y dimensions equal. 3D convolutions: X, Y, Z dimensions equal: randomly applies one 24 possible 90° rotations. two spatial dimensions equal: randomly applies one 4 possible 90° rotations plane two spatial dimensions. available 1D convolutions. "flip": Randomly flips spatial dimension independently 50% probability. "noise": Adds small amount normally distributed noise tensor.

code: # \donttest{ if(torch::torch_is_installed()){ library(cito)  # Example workflow in cito  device <- ifelse(torch::cuda_is_available(), "cuda", "cpu")  ## Data ### We generate our own data: ### 320 images (3x50x50) of either rectangles or ellipsoids shapes <- cito:::simulate_shapes(n=320, size=50, channels=3) X <- shapes$data Y <- shapes$labels  ## Architecture ### Declare the architecture of the CNN ### Note that the output layer is added automatically by cnn() architecture <- create_architecture(conv(5), maxPool(), conv(5), maxPool(), linear(10))  ## Build and train network ### cross-entropy (softmax link) for classification cnn.fit <- cnn(X, Y, architecture, loss = "cross-entropy",                epochs = 2, validation = 0.1, lr = 0.05, device=device)  ## The training loss is below the baseline loss but at the end of the ## training the loss was still decreasing, so continue training for another 5 ## epochs cnn.fit <- continue_training(cnn.fit, epochs = 5)  # Structure of Neural Network print(cnn.fit)  # Plot Neural Network plot(cnn.fit)  ## Convergence can be tested via the analyze_training function analyze_training(cnn.fit)  ## Transfer learning ### With the transfer() function we can use predefined architectures with pretrained weights transfer_architecture <- create_architecture(transfer("resnet18")) resnet <- cnn(X, Y, transfer_architecture, loss = "cross-entropy",               epochs = 1, validation = 0.1, lr = 0.05, device=device) print(resnet) plot(resnet) } #> Loss at epoch 1: training: 0.693, validation: 0.699, lr: 0.05000  #> Loss at conditionalEffects(nn.fit)  ## Main effects (categorical features are not supported) ACE  ## With interaction effects: ACE = conditionalEffects(nn.fit, interactions = TRUE) ## The off diagonal title: Create a CNN Architecture — create_architecture
text: ... Objects class citolayer created linear, conv, maxPool, avgPool, transfer. layers define architecture CNN. default_n_neurons (integer) Default number neurons linear layer. Default 10. default_n_kernels (integer) Default number kernels convolutional layer. Default 10. default_kernel_size (integer tuple) Default size kernels convolutional pooling layers. Can single integer tuple sizes differ across dimensions. Default list(conv = 3, maxPool = 2, avgPool = 2). default_stride (integer tuple) Default stride kernels convolutional pooling layers. Can single integer, tuple strides differ across dimensions, NULL use kernel size. Default list(conv = 1, maxPool = NULL, avgPool = NULL). default_padding (integer tuple) Default zero-padding added sides input. Can single integer tuple padding differs across dimensions. Default list(conv = 0, maxPool = 0, avgPool = 0). default_dilation (integer tuple) Default dilation kernels convolutional max pooling layers. Can single integer tuple dilation differs across dimensions. Default list(conv = 1, maxPool = 1). default_bias (boolean) Default value indicating learnable bias added neurons linear layers kernels convolutional layers. Default list(conv = TRUE, linear = TRUE). default_activation (character) Default activation function used linear convolutional layers. Supported activation functions include "relu", "leaky_relu", "tanh", "elu", "rrelu", "prelu", "softplus", "celu", "selu", "gelu", "relu6", "sigmoid", "softsign", "hardtanh", "tanhshrink", "softshrink", "hardshrink", "log_sigmoid". Default list(conv = "relu", linear = "relu"). default_normalization (boolean) Default value indicating batch normalization applied linear convolutional layers. Default list(conv = FALSE, linear = FALSE). default_dropout (numeric) Default dropout rate linear convolutional layers. Set 0 dropout. Default list(conv = 0.0, linear = 0.0).

title: Create a CNN Architecture — create_architecture
code: # \donttest{ if(torch::torch_is_installed()){ library(cito)  # Convolutional layers with different n_kernels and kernel_sizes c1 <- conv(n_kernels = 8, kernel_size = 5) c2 <- conv(n_kernels = 16, kernel_size = 3)  # Linear layer l <- linear(n_neurons = 100)  # MaxPooling layer mP <- maxPool(kernel_size = 2)  # Create the architecture by using the created layers # Change the defaults with which the not assigned layer parameters will be filled e.g. # change default dropout to different values for linear and convolutional layer # only change the default normalization for linear layers # change default activation of both linear and convolutional layers to 'selu' architecture <- create_architecture(c1, c1, mP, c2, c2, mP, l,                                     default_dropout = list(linear=0.6, conv=0.4),                                     default_normalization = list(linear=TRUE),                                     default_activation = "selu")  # See how the finished CNN would look like for specific input and output shapes print(architecture, c(3,128,128), 10)  # To use predefined architectures  use the transfer() layer alexnet <- transfer("alexnet")  # No other linear layers are used after the transfer layer: # The cnn() function will replace the linear classifier of the # alexnet architecture with a single linear output layer architecture <- create_architecture(alexnet) print(architecture, c(3,128,128), 10)  # Some linear layers are used after the transfer layer: # The cnn() function will replace the linear classifier of the alexnet architecture # with the specified linear layers + an output layer that matches the output dimensions architecture <- create_architecture(alexnet, linear(300), linear(100)) print(architecture, code: # \donttest{  if(torch::torch_is_installed()){ library(cito)  # Example workflow in cito  ## Build and train  Network ### cross-entropy (softmax link) for multi-class responses (e.g., Species) nn.fit<- dnn(Species~., data = datasets::iris, loss = "cross-entropy")  ## The training loss is below the baseline loss but at the end of the ## training the loss was still decreasing, so continue training for another 50 ## epochs nn.fit <- continue_training(nn.fit, epochs = 50L)  # Structure of Neural Network print(nn.fit)  # Plot Neural Network if(requireNamespace("ggraph", quietly = TRUE)) plot(nn.fit, plot_type = "arch") ## 4 Input nodes (first layer) because of 4 features ## 3 Output nodes (last layer) because of 3 response species (one node for each ## level in the response variable). ## The layers between the input and output layer are called hidden layers (two ## of them)  ## We now want to understand how the predictions are made, what are the ## important features? The summary function automatically calculates feature ## importance (the interpretation is similar to an anova) and calculates ## average conditional effects that are similar to linear effects: summary(nn.fit)  ## To visualize the effect (response-feature effect), we can use the ALE and ## PDP functions  # Partial dependencies PDP(nn.fit, variable = "Petal.Length")  # Accumulated local effect plots ALE(nn.fit, variable = "Petal.Length")    # Per se, it is difficult to get confidence intervals for our xAI metrics (or # for the predictions). But we can use bootstrapping to obtain uncertainties # for all cito outputs: ## Re-fit the neural network with bootstrapping nn.fit<- dnn(Species~.,              data = datasets::iris,              loss = "cross-entropy",              epochs = 150L,              verbose = FALSE,              bootstrap = 20L) ## convergence can be tested via the analyze_training function analyze_training(nn.fit)  ## Summary for xAI metrics (can take some time): summary(nn.fit, importance = "permutation", type = "link") ## Now with standard errors and p-values ## Note: Take the p-values with a grain of salt! We do not know yet if they are ## correct (e.g. if you use regularization, they are likely conservative == too ## large)  ## Predictions with bootstrapping: dim(predict(nn.fit)) ## predictions are by default averaged (over the bootstrap samples)  ## Multinomial and conditional logit regression m = dnn(Species~., data = iris, loss = "clogit", lr = 0.01) m = dnn(Species~., data = iris, loss = "multinomial", lr = 0.01)  Y = t(stats::rmultinom(100, 10, prob = c(0.2, 0.2, 0.5))) m = dnn(cbind(X1, X2, X3)~., data = data.frame(Y, A = as.factor(runif(100))),         loss = "multinomial", lr = 0.01) ## conditional logit for size > 1 is not supported yet   # Hyperparameter tuning (experimental feature) hidden_values = matrix(c(5, 2,                          4, 2,                          10,2,                          15,2), 4, 2, byrow = TRUE) ## Potential architectures we want to test, first column == number of nodes print(hidden_values)  nn.fit = dnn(Species~.,              data = iris,              epochs = 30L,              loss = "cross-entropy",              hidden = tune(values = hidden_values),              lr = tune(0.00001, 0.1) # tune lr between range 0.00001 and 0.1              ) ## Tuning results: print(nn.fit$tuning)  # test = Inf means that tuning was cancelled after only one fit (within the CV)   # Advanced: Custom loss functions and additional parameters ## Normal Likelihood with sd parameter: custom_loss = function(pred, true) {   logLik = torch::distr_normal(pred,                                scale = torch::nnf_relu(scale)+                                  0.001)$log_prob(true)   return(-logLik$mean()) }  nn.fit<- dnn(Sepal.Length~.,              data = datasets::iris,              loss = custom_loss,              verbose = FALSE,              custom_parameters = list(scale = 1.0) ) nn.fit$loss$parameters$scale  ## Multivariate normal likelihood with parametrized covariance matrix ## Sigma = L*L^t + D ## Helper function to build covariance matrix create_cov = function(LU, Diag) {   return(torch::torch_matmul(LU, LU$t()) + torch::torch_diag(Diag$exp()+0.01)) }  custom_loss_MVN = function(true, pred) {   Sigma = create_cov(SigmaPar, SigmaDiag)   logLik = torch::distr_multivariate_normal(pred,                                             covariance_matrix = Sigma)$     log_prob(true)   return(-logLik$mean()) }   nn.fit<- dnn(cbind(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, Petal.Length)~.,              data = datasets::iris,              lr = 0.01,              verbose = FALSE,              loss = custom_loss_MVN,              custom_parameters =                list(SigmaDiag =  rep(0, 3),                     SigmaPar = matrix(rnorm(6, sd = 0.001), 3, 2)) ) as.matrix(create_cov(nn.fit$loss$parameters$SigmaPar,                      nn.fit$loss$parameters$SigmaDiag))   # Embeddings and fixed effects ## Species enters as an embedding: each species gets two learned coordinates, ## from which the network learns how the species differ in their response to ## all predictors. Petal.Width enters as a fixed (linear) effect. nn.fit = dnn(Sepal.Length ~ Sepal.Width + Petal.Length + fe(Petal.Width) + e(Species, dim = 2),              data = datasets::iris, loss = "mse", epochs = 50L, verbose = FALSE)  ## the linear effect of Petal.Width coef(nn.fit)$fixed_effects  ## the embeddings, one row per species coef(nn.fit)$net_parameters$e_1.weight  ## architecture: Species feeds its two embedding dimensions, Petal.Width goes ## straight to the output if(requireNamespace("ggraph", quietly = TRUE)) plot(nn.fit, plot_type = "arch") } #> Loss at epoch 1: 0.987150, lr: 0.01000  #> code: # \donttest{ if(torch::torch_is_installed()){  # The following example shows that groups with similar responses will cluster in embedding space set.seed(123)  n = 10000 # observations m = 100 # groups / individuals k = 10 # cluster of groups with the same behavior  dat = data.frame(f1 = runif(n),                  f2 = runif(n),                  f3 = runif(n),                  ind = factor(rep(1:m, each = n/m)),                  cluster = rep(1:k, each = n/k),                  response = NA)  slopes = matrix(runif(3*k, min = -10,max = 10), nrow = k, ncol = 3)  for(i in 1:k) dat$response[dat$cluster == i] =   as.matrix(dat[dat$cluster == i, 1:3]) %*% slopes[i,] + rnorm(n/k, sd = 0.2)  mod <- dnn(response~f1+f2+f3 + e(ind,dim = 2),            data = dat, epochs = 200L, optimizer = config_optimizer("adam"))  embeddings = coef(mod)[[1]][[1]] # extract embeddings plot(embeddings, col = c(rep(1:k, each = m/k))) # plot clusters in embedding space abline(h = 0, lty = 2) abline(v = 0, lty = 2)  ace = conditionalEffects(mod) # extract conditional effects # now average conditional effects per cluster ind_ace =   sapply(1:m, function(ind) {     tmp = ace[[1]]$result[dat$ind==ind,,]     return(diag(apply(tmp, 2:3, mean)))   })  # to create biplot, multiply beta of each cluster with coordinates coord = ind_ace %*% embeddings/m arrows(x0 = rep(0, 3), code: # \donttest{ if(torch::torch_is_installed()){ library(cito)  # linear effects of Temp and Temp^2, a non-linear effect of X1 learned by the DNN set.seed(42) n = 1000 dat = data.frame(X1 = runif(n, -2, 2), Temp = rnorm(n), Precp = rnorm(n)) dat$Y = sin(2 * dat$X1) + 1.0 * dat$Temp - 0.5 * dat$Temp^2 + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3)  m = dnn(Y ~ X1 + fe(Temp + I(Temp^2)), data = dat, loss = "mse", epochs = 50L, verbose = FALSE)  # the fixed effects, close to 1.0 and -0.5 coef(m)$fixed_effects  # "." uses every variable that is not in fe(); here X1 and Precp m2 = dnn(Y ~ . + fe(Temp + I(Temp^2), lambda = 0.001), data = dat, loss = "mse",          epochs = 50L, verbose = FALSE) }   # }

code: mmn(   formula,   dataList = NULL,   fusion_hidden = c(50L, 50L),   fusion_activation = "relu",   fusion_bias = TRUE,   fusion_dropout = 0,   loss = c("mse", "mae", "cross-entropy", "bernoulli", "gaussian", "binomial", "poisson",     "mvp", "nbinom", "multinomial", "clogit", "softmax"),   custom_parameters = NULL,   optimizer = c("sgd", "adam", "adadelta", "adagrad", "rmsprop", "rprop", "ignite_adam"),   lr = 0.01,   lr_scheduler = NULL,   alpha = 0.5,   lambda = 0,   validation = 0,   batchsize = NULL,   shuffle = TRUE,   data_augmentation = NULL,   epochs = 100,   weights = NULL,   early_stopping = Inf,   burnin = Inf,   baseloss = NULL,   device = c("cpu", "cuda", "mps"),   plot = TRUE,   verbose = TRUE )

title: Train a Multi-Modal Neural Network (MMN) — mmn
text: formula formula object specifying model structure. See examples information. dataList list containing data training model. list contain variables used formula. fusion_hidden numeric vector specifying number units (nodes) hidden layer fusion network. length vector determines number hidden layers created, element specifying number units corresponding layer. fusion_activation character vector specifying activation function(s) applied hidden layer fusion network. single character string provided, activation function applied hidden layers. Alternatively, character vector length fusion_hidden can provided apply different activation functions layer. Available options include: "relu", "leaky_relu", "tanh", "elu", "rrelu", "prelu", "softplus", "celu", "selu", "gelu", "relu6", "sigmoid", "softsign", "hardtanh", "tanhshrink", "softshrink", "hardshrink", "log_sigmoid". fusion_bias logical value vector indicating whether include bias terms layer fusion network. single logical value provided, apply layers. specify bias inclusion layer individually, provide logical vector length length(fusion_hidden) + 1, element corresponds hidden layer, final element controls whether bias term added output layer. fusion_dropout dropout rate(s) apply hidden layer fusion network. can single numeric value (0 1) apply dropout rate hidden layers, numeric vector length length(fusion_hidden) set different dropout rates layer individually. dropout rate applied output layer. loss loss function used. Options include "mse", "mae", "cross-entropy", "bernoulli", "gaussian", "binomial", "poisson", "nbinom", "mvp", "multinomial", "clogit". can also specify loss function. See Details information. Default "mse". custom_parameters Parameters custom loss function. See vignette example. Default NULL. optimizer optimizer used. Options include "sgd", "adam", "adadelta", "adagrad", "rmsprop", "rprop", "ignite_adam". See config_optimizer adjustments optimizer. Default "sgd". lr Learning rate optimizer. Default 0.01. lr_scheduler Learning rate scheduler. See config_lr_scheduler creating learning rate scheduler. Default NULL. alpha Alpha value L1/L2 regularization. Default 0.5. lambda Lambda value L1/L2 regularization. Default 0.0. validation Proportion data used validation. Alternatively, vector containing indices validation samples can provided. Default 0.0. batchsize Batch size training. NULL, batchsize 10% training data. Default NULL. shuffle Whether shuffle data epoch. Default TRUE. data_augmentation list functions used data augmentation. Elements must either functions strings corresponding inbuilt data augmentation functions. See details information. epochs Number epochs train model. Default 100. weights weights values (can also matrix) likelihood access . early_stopping Number epochs improvement training stopped. Default Inf. burnin Number epochs training stops loss still baseloss. Default Inf. baseloss Baseloss used burnin plot. NULL, baseloss corresponds intercept models. Default NULL. device Device used training. Options "cpu", "cuda", "mps". Default "cpu". plot Whether plot training progress. Default TRUE. verbose Whether print detailed training progress. Default TRUE.

title: Train a Multi-Modal Neural Network (MMN) — mmn
text: S3 object class "citommn" returned. list containing everything know model training process. list consists following attributes: net object class "nn_module". Originates torch package represents core object workflow. call original function call. loss object class "nn_module". Contains relevant information loss function, e.g. parameters function (format_Y) transforms target data. data list. Contains data used training model. model_properties list properties, define architecture model. training_properties list training hyperparameters used last time model trained. losses data.frame containing training validation losses epoch. best_epoch_net_state_dict Serialized state dict net best training epoch. best_epoch_loss_state_dict Serialized state dict loss best training epoch. last_epoch_net_state_dict Serialized state dict net last training epoch. last_epoch_loss_state_dict Serialized state dict loss last training epoch. use_model_epoch String, either "best" "last". Determines whether parameters (e.g. weights, biases) best last training epoch used (e.g. prediction). loaded_model_epoch String, shows training epoch parameters currently loaded net loss.

title: Train a Multi-Modal Neural Network (MMN) — mmn
text: MMN combines multiple CNNs DNNs. allows model process data different formats (e.g., DNN+CNN tabular data images, CNN+CNN images different spatial resolutions). architecture MMN defined arguments formula, fusion_hidden, fusion_activation, fusion_bias fusion_dropout: formula specifies architecture individual networks well respective inputs, target data MMN (specifies shape output layer). fusion_hidden, fusion_activation, fusion_bias fusion_dropout define architecture DNN fuses outputs individual networks. See dnn details. mmn(Y ~ dnn(X=tabular_data1) + dnn(~., data=tabular_data2) + cnn(X=image_data), dataList=mmn_data, ...) example, Y (left side ~) target data MMN. right side ~ can specify many DNNs CNNs required. specification works exactly dnn cnn following restrictions: specify arguments relate architecture input data network (bold arguments mandatory): dnn(): formula, data, hidden, activation, bias, dropout, (X, alternatively formula data) cnn(): X, architecture Arguments relating training (e.g. loss, lr, epochs, ...) passed mmn() instead. names data variables (example: Y, tabular_data1, tabular_data2, image_data) must available dataList (named list).

title: Train a Multi-Modal Neural Network (MMN) — mmn
text: Armin Schenk

title: Train a Multi-Modal Neural Network (MMN) — mmn
code: # \donttest{ if(torch::torch_is_installed()){ library(cito)  # Example workflow in cito  device <- ifelse(torch::cuda_is_available(), "cuda", "cpu")  ## Simulated data shapes <- cito:::simulate_shapes(n=320, size=50, channels=3) X_cnn <- shapes$data X_dnn <- matrix(runif(320*3),320,3) Y <- (as.integer(shapes$labels)-1)*2 + 0.5*X_dnn[,1] + 0.3*X_dnn[,2] - 0.8*X_dnn[,3]  data <- list(Y=Y, X_cnn=X_cnn, X_dnn=X_dnn)  ## Architecture of the CNN architecture <- create_architecture(conv(5), maxPool(), conv(5), maxPool(), linear(10))  ## Build and train network mmn.fit <- mmn(Y ~                  dnn(~., data=X_dnn, hidden = c(100,100,100), activation = "relu") +                  cnn(X=X_cnn, architecture = architecture),                dataList = data, loss = "mse",                epochs = 1, validation = 0.1, lr = 0.05, device=device)  ## If the loss is still decreasing you can continue training for additional epochs: mmn.fit <- continue_training(mmn.fit, epochs = 1) } #> Loss at epoch 1: training: 1.618, validation: 1.594, lr: 0.05000  #> Loss at epoch 2: training: 1.132, validation: 1.280, lr: 0.05000  # }

title: Predict with a fitted CNN model — predict.citocnn
text: object model created cnn. newdata multidimensional array representing new data predictions made. dimensions newdata match training data, except first dimension represents number samples. alternative, can provide relative absolute path folder containing images. case, unsigned integer images divided maximum value (255 8 bit, 65535 16 bit), floating point signed integer TIFFs passed unchanged. Windows raster given raster_patches (use like argument, carry preprocessing training windows); rescaled. NULL, function uses data model trained . type character string specifying type prediction made. Options : "link": Scale linear predictor. "response": Scale response. "class": predicted class labels (classification tasks). device Device used making predictions. Options "cpu", "cuda", "mps". NULL, function uses device used training model. Default NULL. batchsize integer specifying number samples processed time. NULL, function uses batchsize used training model. Default NULL. return_embeddings Return embeddings instead predictions ... Additional arguments (currently used).

code: # \donttest{ if(torch::torch_is_installed() && cito:::cito_decoder_available()[["tiff"]]){ library(cito)  # a small georeferenced raster stands in for a large satellite scene f = system.file("extdata", "raster.tif", package = "cito") coords = cbind(x = runif(200, 600100, 600900), y = runif(200, 5300100, 5300700)) # log-transform, then standardize every band with the mean and sd over the windows; # missing pixels become 0 (the mean) and are flagged in an extra channel X = raster_patches(f, coords, extent = 200, transform = function(x) torch::torch_log1p(x),                    standardize = TRUE, na_channel = TRUE) X # the first four windows as the network sees them: [windows, channels, height, width] dim(as.array(X[1:4])) Y = matrix(rnorm(200), ncol = 1)  nn.fit = cnn(X = X, Y = Y, loss = "mse", epochs = 2L, batchsize = 32L,              architecture = create_architecture(conv(4), maxPool(), linear(10)))  # new sites, with the preprocessing of the training windows new_coords = cbind(x = runif(5, 600100, 600900), y = runif(5, 5300100, 5300700)) predict(nn.fit, newdata = raster_patches(coords = new_coords, like = X)) } #> Loss at epoch 1: 1.049537, lr: 0.01000  #> Loss at epoch 2: 1.041751, lr: 0.01000 #>             [,1] #> [1,] -0.02080041 #> [2,] -0.01961719 #> [3,] -0.01359830 #> [4,] -0.01831388 #> [5,] -0.01849026 # }

text: summary reports feature importance (following Fisher, Rudin, Dominici, 2018) together mean standard deviation average conditional effects (following Pichler & Hartig, 2023). Feature importances interpreted similarly ANOVA: main interaction effects absorbed individual features. also sensitive collinearity features, .e. two features collinear, importances may overestimated. Average conditional effects (ACE) similar marginal effects approximate linear effects, .e. interpretation similar coefficients linear regression model. standard deviation ACE quantifies non-linearity feature effect: higher values indicate stronger non-linearities. permutation importance, loss model evaluated original permuted feature (\(e_{perm}\) \(e_{orig}\)), importance feature j reported relative increase \(FI_j = e_{perm}/e_{orig} - 1\). "ale" "ce" importances derived conditional effects therefore defined numerical features; categorical features left importance table (message says ).
